reviews.text: In these times when people see more differences than similarities, it feels important to remember that even when you probably don’t like most people you meet, we are the only thing we have for each other.
reviews.author: Nelson Acosta

reviews.text: a devious film in that it’s just barely mysterious and intriguing enough that you want some kind of explanation, no matter how obvious it becomes that the explanation is going to be incredibly stupid.
reviews.author: William Schwartz

reviews.text: The most insolent executive-office musing ever committed to film -- a full-out assault on the nation’s people.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: The tension is breathless and well-constructed, but since they begin with the dial at eleven, there is nowhere to go throughout the film’s exhausting 140 minutes.
reviews.author: Lillian Crawford

reviews.text: The film has more impossible shots than the Harlem Globetrotters.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is barely a blip. There are only mildly interesting ideas, but they have all been done better previously and likely will be done better in the future. Esmail’s film is all style, no substance, and a waste of talent.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: Director/Writer Esmail has fashioned an end-of-the-world storyline that keeps pounding our fears throughout its 140 minutes.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: Doesn’t just offer disheartening disaster sequences, it is also a thought-provoking journey into the complexities of our contemporary existence; the type of film we don’t get enough of these days.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: This is why I always tell my kids to download sh*t to their devices. I'm not paying for airplane wifi.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is thankfully as intriguing as it sounds, with fantastic tension building and strong performances. However, it's failure to stick the landing and over-explaining of the obvious gives it a disappointing conclusion.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: A complex apocalyptic thriller that's ominous and pessimistic, but also thought-provoking and entertaining. It’s the type of film that begs for a lengthy discussion afterwards.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: To say that the film delivers an ever-tightening sense of dread is an understatement. The acting is about as good as what you'd expect from such a high-powered cast, but I was especially taken with Farrah Mackenzie.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: The mystery of what is happening is resolved in dribs and drabs and never completely; the script has an abundance of trickery. In the end, some will wonder if there will be a second chapter; This could pass for a pilot episode.
reviews.author: Ricardo De Querol

reviews.text: This is an oft-repeated world-is-coming-to-an-end plot that goes around many circles and gets lost in the loop of confusion, leaving you with more questions than answers in the end.
reviews.author: Ronak Kotecha

reviews.text: That Leave the World Behind offers so many questions and few answers — at least of the easy variety — means it probably isn’t for everyone, but it should be experienced by many.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Shyamalan meets Black Mirror in this hugely entertaining, visually inventive apocalyptic thriller with a killer ending.
reviews.author: Farah Cheded

reviews.text: The most appealing aspect of Leave the World Behind is watching the fear taking hold of these characters while they desperately try to rationalize and explain everything that’s happening around them.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: The film is a cautionary tale on the fragility of society, about classism and racism and other mechanisms that can be used to cause friction and disunity. It leaves the viewer to reflect upon an ominous message about where the world might be heading.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: It doesn't so much as end as just stop.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: ... The film boldly sets itself in a post-conspiracy-theories space as its mysterious elite confesses to losing control. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan José Beteta

reviews.text: …Leave the World Behind is a handsome looking production, with a big-name cast and lots of weird sideways visuals to create a disconcerting mood that never pays off; the ending is glib and means less than zero…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind downplays Alam’s magical realism to deliver a more grounded account of the unravelling of present-day America.
reviews.author: Rich Cross

reviews.text: The apocalyptic drama Leave the World Behind isn't really about any faraway, unknown enemies responsible for the attack. It's more about how people respond to a crisis when they think enemies are closer to home.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Deathless quote: “I am a man without GPS and a phone. I am a useless man”. Ain’t it the truth?
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: An apocalyptic "Big Mystery" movie with an ending that's sort of a troll. But it's a good troll.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: The slow pace of the movie helps build the tension and make everything nerve-wracking. The framing and camera work really added creativity to the direction.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: If this is the kind of streaming "content" we'd lose in an internet destroying apocalypse, maybe we'd be better off.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Writer/director Sam Esmail delivers a hypnotic, yet patient (sometimes to a fault), apocalyptic thriller.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: The end of the world is always a valuable thought experiment; it makes us start asking important questions. Alam’s book wondered: “What if?” But Esmail’s movie mostly wants to know: “How come?”
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Well-executed apocalyptic thriller will no doubt spark considerable debate. Be prepared to be thinking about bunkers for days afterwards.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: It's not subtle, but Esmail's direction, Julia Roberts playing unlikeable and the lack of reassuring closure or answers makes LEAVE THE WORLD BEHIND an entertaining, albeit overlong, thriller.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: We’re not in control, but Sam Esmail is of his startling, character-driven doomsday story about what happens when there’s the very real possibility everything is about to end.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Fully equipped with an excellent ensemble cast and a nail-biting script, Sam Esmail delivers a knock-out of a thriller.
reviews.author: Jon Mendelsohn

reviews.text: Filmed with a catalog of trite or banal shots, the film sprawls between pirouettes without fully capturing tension until its final stretch. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: Yet one more film that confuses the Apocalypse with Dystopia...
reviews.author: Charles Mudede

reviews.text: Leave The World Behind plays off of questioning mystery without the satisfaction of developing the central conflict or offering substantial answers about what happens to the main characters.
reviews.author: Lindsay Press

reviews.text: Beautiful, but slow, sci-fi fantasy set against the backdrop of a cyberattack and piracy of an America fried by its technological advancements. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Netflix original serves up constant dread, garbled statements about modern life.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: The filmmakers masterfully balance the need for suspense without alienating the audience, resulting in a viewing experience that is intriguing.
reviews.author: Tatat Bunnag

reviews.text: Netflix's "Leave the World Behind" depicts world's end as an event that unleashes collective paranoia rather than a catastrophe. The result is a film that gives very little explanation and creates a rich soil for all kinds of theories.
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: Tautly executed – it’s 138-minute running time flies by – and terrifyingly timely, this cautionary tale is one that should be heeded. Yet, in the end, it suggests that we’re already doomed.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The world is ending, again, and the excellent ensemble and sneaky camerawork combine for a suspenseful contribution to the overcrowded doomsday genre.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: In its desperation for prestige — director Sam Esmail gives himself the rather narcissistic ‘written for the screen and directed by’ credit — it sacrifices the pulp at its core.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: An absolute corker...Performances are terrific, with Julia Roberts especially interesting with the hint her character might have a problem with black people. Providing strong support  Kevin Bacon steps in with a pungent cameo as a diehard survivalist.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: This is a tense, psychological thriller about trust, and about how do you survive a potential ending of the world. A fantastic cast.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: As a Netflix release, this feels akin to sitting around on a Saturday night to watch The Day After on TV. On top of that, you have a terrific cast being pushed to certain limits in manners that effectively create tension from within.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: An ambiguously suspenseful, escapist/doomsday scenario that's cleverly cast and executed.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Sam Esmail’s Leave the World Behind is a Master Class in Filmmaking
reviews.author: Jeanine T. Abraham

reviews.text: For a cast this talented, and a visual palette willing to take chances, we come away feeling like we ran around in circles with nothing to show for it.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Leave The World Behind is a wackadoodle apocalypse movie, both self-serious to a hilarious fault and very in on the joke.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Director/co-screenwriter Sam Esmail (Mr. Robot) sets up the film with an M. Night Shyamalan vibe — as good and, at times great, as it gets — it’s all going to come down to how it ends.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: While its satire feels pedestrian and its mystery ultimately lacking, Esmail crafts an engaging enough narrative propped up by captivating performances...
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: I find it ironic that Leave The World Behind is split into 4 Acts when the entire movie never gets past the opening. This is an absolute chore to site through with zero payoff at the end.
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text: The film is an audacious mash-up of Get Out, Esmail’s Mr Robot and all those paranoid 1970s thrillers...
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Not everyone will appreciate the apocalytic world director/writer Sam Esmail has created here, but the material is resonant and the cast is exceptional enough to recommend.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Conspiracy theories are always appealing... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: With such an arch depiction of well-off characters flailing in a moment of crisis, it almost feels like a companion piece to both The White Lotus and Triangle of Sadness.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: One can read good faith into the film’s consternation over the ways we are susceptible to generalizations and othering those we disagree with, while also observing Leave the World Behind is inadvertently guilty of the very same thing.
reviews.author: Andrew Dignan

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is one of the best surprises of the year and a MUST WATCH on Netflix.
reviews.author: Shahbaz Siddiqui

reviews.text: Fantastic performances from all four leads, an apocalyptic story about a world without technology that's also surprisingly a love letter to physical media.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: Not everything in the film works, but a great deal of it does, and it certainly dares to go darker than most films do about the potential collapse of civilization.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text:
A sharp script with relatable characters, stylized direction and great actors disconnect us from the world and glue us to the screen.
[Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Crafting a haunting thriller that ruthlessly intertwines shock and despair is an art, and Leave the World Behind revels in this with admirable finesse.
reviews.author: Kristy Strouse

reviews.text: This is Knock at the Cabin, only not as good. All of Esmail’s efforts have been done in every M. Night Shyamalan film already and share the same problems of not knowing how to end.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: A refreshing proposal that is not afraid to capture the hopelessness of the sick world in which we live... [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Sam Esmail’s new film is a disquieting exploration into what it might be like to suddenly lose the creature comforts people take for granted — and, worse, to find out there is a rather terrifying and inescapable reason for it.
reviews.author: Rick Romancito

reviews.text: But “Leave the World Behind” builds slowly to a small denouement, not a big awesome moment, an approach that may frustrate viewers looking for answers. It is best to just appreciate each odd scene for what it is.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: [A]n ambitious and well-acted psychological thriller with apocalyptic tones.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: A fantastically unnerving story brought to life by vibrant and raw performances and drawing on a timely plot. This is one of those movies that sneaks up on you and needles your senses with how tremendously gripping it’s executed.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is shameless manipulation that wields provocation like a shotgun blast. It drove me nuts.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: There is a lot to be desired with its resolution, but the ensemble is excellent, and there is a haunting atmosphere that will leave many unnerved.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: America’s sweetheart [Julia Roberts] has sprinted over to the dark side, and it’s a thrill to see what she does with it.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Whatever one takes away from it, Leave the World Behind should trigger conversations beyond whether to hit the “like” button. By that measure, give Esmail credit for a movie that up, down or sideways, makes it hard to look away.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Whilst the film understands the general mechanics of the post-apocalyptic genre, it is lacking in action.
reviews.author: Romey Norton

reviews.text: “Netflix satire on Netflix” has already been done — and done far better — in Black Mirror Season 6.
reviews.author: Dais Johnston

reviews.text: The film’s ambiguity is both fascinating and frustrating. As uneasy interactions fuel subtle power struggles within the house, we realize the characters are not as compelling as what’s going on around them.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: In the end, Leave the World Behind is content to blandly shrug in the direction of an amorphous calamity, reaching for a profundity that it fails to achieve.
reviews.author: Steven Nguyen Scaife

reviews.text: Based on the novel by Rumaan Alam and boasting a number of terrific set pieces, it’s a creepy, suspenseful and unsettling thriller about human behaviour in the face of the unknown.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind intricately intertwines Sam Esmail’s directorial finesse with Rumaan Alam’s thought-provoking novel, delivering a compelling exploration of familial dynamics, societal issues, and the impact of fear and uncertainty on human behavior
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Esmail uses the story’s ambiguity almost like a get-out-of-jail-free card, piling on the weird events without actually telling us what’s happening. He half-asses it, in other words.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Yet despite Leave the World Behind's early thrills, its gradual loss of momentum leeches any suspense inherent in the film's conceit, resulting in an apocalypse flick that is fine, but nowhere near as insightful as it thinks it is.
reviews.author: Belen Edwards

reviews.text: On paper, everything suggests a thriller in the style of M. Night Shyamalan, and there is some of that, but Esmail does not limit himself and offers a stimulating vision of everything that surrounds a possible end of the world. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: It’s far from an uplifting film, but the acting, the story, and the filmmaking make it highly watchable nonetheless.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Leave The World Behind is a very engaging film. I didn’t feel a second of its 141-minute-long running time. From start to finish, Sam Esmail keeps you hooked to your small screen.
reviews.author: Pramit Chatterjee

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is a film of mysteries and horrors, some of which are all the more unnerving for being difficult, or even impossible, to perceive from the characters’ cocooned vantage point.
reviews.author: Oli Welsh

reviews.text: This genre-defying treat quickly uncoils into something provocative, insightful, chilling, and even darkly funny at times.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: It plays like an M. Night Shyamalan movie, but without the supernatural element and with a thick vein of social critique running throughout. What happens may be extreme, but it feels based on mundane reality.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Leave The World Behind is a thrilling work of apocalyptic tension, utilizing a stellar cast & Netflix budget to widen the breadth of the novel.
reviews.author: Graeme Guttmann

reviews.text: Like the novel it's based on, the movie does not offer any easy answers. For those willing to go along with it though, Leave the World Behind is a gripping, unique and superbly performed thriller.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: Although incredibly well acted and directed, Leave the World Behind, unfortunately, doesn’t have that much new to say about its topic that other films haven’t covered before.
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: A solid psychological thriller elevated by a great cast and fantastic camera work. An unsettling, gripping slow-dance with end-of-the-world implications. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: It establishes a very creepy, uneasy tone but thematically “Leave the World Behind” tries to cover a bit too much ground.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: The performances are the reason to watch, as everyone, young folks included, delivers heartfelt (and sometimes comic, too) turns. But ultimately, this feels a bit like watered-down Sartre.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: As a dread-stoked chamber-piece, Leave the World Behind is gripping. Esmail captures indelible images that (sometimes literally) crash his themes into one another.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: An apocalyptic thriller where a series of cataclysmic events don't add up to much of anything, really.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Favouring family clashes over fearsome set pieces, this dystopian drama wins points for ambition, mood, and Julia Roberts’ prickly performance.
reviews.author: Kate Stables

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind, director Sam Esmail's bleak and chilling new apocalyptic thriller, may make you want to build a bunker.
reviews.author: Sarah McIntyre

reviews.text: I guess you could classify this as a kind of disaster film, but Esmail has created a quirky, self-contained little saga that occasionally hints at something much, much larger lurking in the margins.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Esmail's not as confident with the overall experience of anxiety, keeping “Leave the World Behind” overlong and underwhelming with personal interactions, making for a frustratingly uneven viewing experience.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind bites off more it can chew without making us care too hard about what its saying.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Esmail's screenplay, unfortunately, never quite makes these characters feel like real people caught up in the midst of a technology-free apocalypse...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is an elegant post-apocalyptic film that asks far more questions than it answers. It is thought provoking, but the ending (which I loved) may leave some viewers wishing for more.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Though the main cast are accomplished, beautiful and intermittently interesting, they feel out of place in a movie that ought to have been a lot more scary, or a lot more subdued.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: A peculiar, apocalyptic psychological thriller that relies on excellent direction and exceptional performances. Although the mystery of what is happening is familiar, the human behavior aspects were highly compelling.
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: It’s an unsettling, well-acted experience with layers and cautionary warnings to spare.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Sam Esmail’s film is a dreary, harrowing sit -- and all the more invigorating for it.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: The seeds of our destruction have already been planted by us... And the more that Leave the World Behind pokes at that notion, the more you fear that this isn’t a thriller. It could be a documentary with movie stars.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is a dumb movie disguised as a smart movie, a middling thriller whose decorated cast and tricky camerawork can’t compensate for its undercooked, overwritten script.
reviews.author: Dylan Roth

reviews.text: A solid end-of-world mystery thriller with a strong sense of dread throughout that reflects on how we approach interpersonal relationships and rely on electronic info.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: “Leave the World Behind” struggles where it matters most, fashioning real stakes to accompany the turmoil.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: “Leave the World Behind” showcases the things society takes for granted while also offering insightful commentary on conspiracy theories, perceptions of race, and political turmoil.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: A perfectly cast film that doesn’t skip a beat. Leave the World Behind offers a stellar mix of thrills, unsettling ideas and pitch perfect laughs that amount to a wildly riveting watch, one that will weigh heavily on minds after the credits.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Although at times it seems to veer into its own uncertain logic which yields moments of confusion, Leave the World Behind will undoubtedly lead to passionate debates about the futuristic implications it proposes. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Pablo Russo

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind had a brilliantly squirmy premise that was swiftly squandered on a routine end-of-the world plot filleted from Stephen King door-stoppers like Under the Dome and The Stand.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The acting is first rate and it needs to be -- this is a drama of manners and secrets, and each sigh or glance reveals so much. We haven’t seen a nasty Roberts character in a while and Ali balances sophistication and slyness artfully.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: A wickedly well-crafted piece of pressure-cooker psychology and perhaps not purely speculative havoc.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Despite a highly capable cast that plays each thematic note on cue, Leave the World Behind buckles under the weight of its expanding scale and its many malformed ideas.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The better version of "Leave the World Behind" might not even need to be more of a taut thriller that gets to the finish line while viewers are still engaged with the mystery — it would just need to have the courage of its B-movie convictions.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: ... Almost always interesting and at times straightforwardly devastating. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is a smart, compelling take on the end of the world, and proves Esmail is a writer-director who deserves larger-scale projects like this after his television successes.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: Making crafty use of editing, music, and composition, this pessimistic thriller is more about human flaws than anything thrilling, but it's so well made that it easily catches us in its grip.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: You should be trying to puzzle out what it all can possibly mean. But after awhile you stop asking and just wait for the next expertly administered jolt.
reviews.author: Tom Gliatto

reviews.text: Oh no—not another doomsday thriller! Yes, but  see how director Sam Esmail, powered by an exceptional all-star cast (Julia Roberts, Ethan Hawke, Mahershala Ali, Kevin Bacon), makes you care about being human while frying your nerves to a frazzle.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Has some dazzling moments, but it's also too long, and loses steam in the last act.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: It suffers from trying to do too many things... But on the whole it's a cut above the sort of films Shyamalan has been trying to do lately.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: A pretty playful and taut thriller that's very small but trying to cram in a bunch of ideas about paranoia, class, misanthropy and the dependence of people on the internet.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind might often have the air of a noughties throwback, but you wouldn’t want it to be a minute more up to date.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: An impressively unnerving film with things to say about race, tech and conspiracy theories.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is not especially original; there are too many other apocalyptic movies around for that. But the film... is especially timely.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Blinded by its own shiny smugness, you may want to leave this film behind.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: A mean, nasty, and cynical apocalyptic parable that stages the quintessential end of the world scenario...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: The performances are flawless and the shooting style sensational.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Sam Esmail presents some spectacular images but the film is at least 25 minutes too long. A Quiet Place (2018) covered broadly similar territory much more deftly.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Dizzying shots signal twists of fate and shifts in the order of things, while some bravura special effects work allows the camera to seamlessly traverse walls and floors in the elaborate abode.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Expertly directly and acted, Leave the World Behind (based on the novel by Rumaan Alam) wastes no time getting you in, and then getting on your nerves.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is an addictive parlour game and a chewy treatise on human behaviour.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A provocative, superbly acted action drama that combines big-hitting ambition and spectacle with just enough humour to temper the whole end-of-civilisation meltdown scenario.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: For more than two hours, we are completely immersed in the filmmaker’s compelling and deeply studied world of dread. It’s unfortunate, then, that the film’s conclusion feels too easy and abrupt...
reviews.author: Sarah-Tai Black

reviews.text: Very often writer-director Sam Esmail will split the dramatic focus between two or even three different crises within the ensemble and the effect is a little self-cancelling. And then …?
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Misanthropy can only carry the movie so far before it gets old.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Hang on. A great end of the world thriller.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: While Leave the World Behind can be too on-the-nose at times, it never fails to be an engrossing and chilling look at a doomsday that we can’t help but catapult ourselves towards.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind feels like what you would get if you took this year’s Knock at the Cabin and knocked the Shyamalan out of it.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Viewers have seen films like Leave the World Behind before, but rarely done to such an accomplished and reasoned degree.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is blinded by its own smugness, fancying itself privy to the secrets of the human condition.
reviews.author: Coleman Spilde

reviews.text: “Leave the World Behind” is the unusual case of a film that starts out bad and gets better. So, if you find that you’re already enjoying yourself, stick with it, because it definitely won’t get any worse.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Esmail’s sophomore feature is akin to sci-fi blockbusters of yesteryear with a light, practically Spielbergian touch and sense of adventure.
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: Esmail’s characters are blinded by a different kind of bourgeois comfort food, one that only comes into focus in the film’s final, biting, and deeply satisfying sequence.
reviews.author: Constance Grady

reviews.text: If nothing else, the film is both well-acted and well-crafted.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Never had I watched a movie where I shook my head and said, “White people…” so many times. It was a shared sentiment.
reviews.author: Stacey Yvonne

reviews.text: “Leave the World Behind” enters the stage as one of the year’s best and no doubt will spark massive amounts of conversation.
reviews.author: Kristen Lopez

reviews.text: Leave the World Behind is destined to be a movie lost in the void of a streaming service that will premiere better, more complex pieces of entertainment shortly after it releases, thus rendering this pointless exercise obsolete.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: Unquestionably, for whatever genre you want to place it in, Leave the World Behind has much to say about the tenuous state of our current planet and the freewheeling technology on which we increasingly rely but which also threatens to consume us.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: The film is able to turn what might literally be the end of the world into a gripping stage play because the four adults are so well-written. Ali steals the show as George.
reviews.author: Christian Zilko

reviews.text: And clocking in at 138 minutes, the film’s pace is leisurely (to say the least) where it has to be tight, leaving “Leave the World Behind” in a kind of no man’s land — too talky to work as a genre film and too ham-handed to offer real insight.
reviews.author: Tom O'Brien

reviews.text: This film feels like a more satisfying version of the not-dissimilarly apocalyptic, but ultimately preposterous “Knock at the Cabin” from earlier this year
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Razor sharp dialogue, direction and performances from Julia Roberts, Mahershala Ali, Ethan Hawke and Mya'la make this psychologically impactful thriller a triumph
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Fine performances help to bolster a problematic picture written and directed by Sam Esmail, adapted from Rumaan Alam’s best-selling novel.
reviews.author: Stephen Farber

reviews.text: A confident, entertaining thriller about two families forced to live together in the middle of nowhere as civilization collapses around them.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

synopsis: In this apocalyptic thriller from award-winning writer and director Sam Esmail (Mr. Robot), Amanda (Academy Award winner Julia Roberts) and her husband Clay (Academy Award nominee Ethan Hawke), rent a luxurious home for the weekend with their kids, Archie (Charlie Evans) and Rose (Farrah Mackenzie). Their vacation is soon upended when two strangers -- G.H. (Academy Award winner Mahershala Ali) and his daughter Ruth (Myha'la) -- arrive in the night, bearing news of a mysterious cyberattack and seeking refuge in the house they claim is theirs. The two families reckon with a looming disaster that grows more terrifying by the minute, forcing everyone to come to terms with their places in a collapsing world.
